name: Avoiding Common White Collar Crime Defense Mistakes

step.name: Step 1: [ ] Mistake: Talking to investigators without an attorney — why: An…
step.text: [ ] Mistake: Talking to investigators without an attorney — why: Anything you say can be used against you, even if you think you're just clarifying details. It's always best to have legal representation present.

step.name: Step 2: [ ] Mistake: Deleting or altering documents or digital files — why:…
step.text: [ ] Mistake: Deleting or altering documents or digital files — why: This can be seen as obstruction of justice, which is a separate and serious charge. Preserve everything as it is.

step.name: Step 3: [ ] Mistake: Not taking the charges seriously enough — why: White c…
step.text: [ ] Mistake: Not taking the charges seriously enough — why: White collar crimes carry severe penalties, including lengthy prison sentences and hefty fines. They're not just 'business disputes.'

step.name: Step 4: [ ] Mistake: Believing you can handle the investigation on your own…
step.text: [ ] Mistake: Believing you can handle the investigation on your own — why: Prosecutors often have months or years of financial records and witness statements. You need a defense strategy that can match that level of preparation.

step.name: Step 5: [ ] Mistake: Delaying seeking legal counsel — why: Early, strategic…
step.text: [ ] Mistake: Delaying seeking legal counsel — why: Early, strategic defense matters immensely in these cases. The sooner you have an attorney, the sooner they can start building your defense, challenging evidence, and protecting your rights.
